nodes.content: Design a restartable device-driver isolation boundary that contains DMA faults without invalidating hard-real-time guarantees for unaffected devices.
requirements: Contain arbitrary driver memory writes, DMA, and interrupt storms across driver crashes and restarts.
Unaffected devices retain verified 1 ms service deadlines during driver faults and concurrent recovery.

nodes.content: Use per-driver MMU/IOMMU domains, remapped maskable interrupts, DMA-quiesce/reset restarts, and budgeted recovery separate from reserved real-time cores.
How can driver DMA and interrupts be revoked during restart without consuming unaffected devices’ reserved 1 ms service budgets?
Recovery-core isolation, interrupt quotas, and IOMMU drain-before-reuse yield zero unaffected 1 ms misses during DMA floods and interrupt storms.
Run 10,000 FaultBench-1 restart trials with rogue writes, stale DMA, and 100-kHz interrupts; measure IOMMU drains and unaffected-device deadline misses.
FaultBench-1: 10,000 storm-driven restarts showed zero cross-domain writes, post-reuse DMA writes, or unaffected-device 1 ms deadline misses.
Adopt per-driver domains, interrupt quotas, recovery-core isolation, and IOMMU drain-before-reuse; FaultBench-1 supports implementation, pending WCET certification.
Implement adopted domains and recovery isolation; bound shared interrupt/IOMMU interference, then certify unaffected-device 1 ms response times during restarts.
Implement DomainGuard v1 with per-driver MMU/IOMMU domains, interrupt-remapping quotas, isolated recovery core, and drain-confirmed DMA buffer reuse.
DomainGuard v1 patchset adds per-driver MMU/IOMMU mappings, interrupt quotas, recovery-core pinning, and drain-gated DMA buffer reuse.
Measure DomainGuard v1’s worst-case interrupt/IOMMU blocking under 100-kHz storms; include bounds in unaffected-device 1 ms response-time analysis.
DomainGuard v1: IOMMU invalidations caused 180 µs maximum shared-fabric blocking and 27 unaffected-device deadline misses during 100-kHz storms.
Revoke driver MMIO, disable bus mastering, quarantine DMA buffers, and schedule IOMMU invalidations in certified slack to eliminate deadline misses.
Implement DomainGuard v2 MMIO revocation, bus-master shutdown, buffer quarantine, and slack-scheduled invalidations; rerun FaultBench-1 and 1 ms response-time analysis.
DomainGuard v2: 10,000 FaultBench-1 restarts yielded zero escaped CPU/DMA writes or deadline misses; certified worst-case response was 0.91 ms.
Run ConcurRecover-2 with simultaneous driver crashes, 100-kHz storms, and delayed DMA; measure quarantine release, invalidation slack, deadline misses.
ConcurRecover-2: four concurrent restarts exceeded certified invalidation slack by 65 µs, causing eight unaffected-device deadline misses; quarantine blocked stale DMA.
Serialize IOMMU invalidations one-per-slack-window; immediate interrupt masking, bus-master shutdown, and DMA quarantine yield zero four-restart deadline misses.
Implement DomainGuard v3’s slack-gated invalidation queue; rerun four-crash ConcurRecover-2, checking stale DMA containment and certified 1 ms bounds.
ConcurRecover-2: four concurrent restarts under 100-kHz storms yielded zero deadline misses or stale-DMA escapes; certified response bound: 0.96 ms.
Stress DomainGuard v3 with four simultaneous crashes and delayed PCIe writes; check DMA quarantine exhaustion and 1 ms deadlines.
Delayed-PCIe stress: four restarts exhausted the 256-page quarantine; shared allocator contention caused three unaffected-device 1 ms deadline misses.
Per-driver quarantine pools and fail-closed restart admission prevent shared-allocator contention while serialized invalidations yield zero four-crash deadline misses.
Audit DomainGuard v3’s serialized invalidations under four crashes and exhausted quarantine; measure interrupt-mask latency and unaffected-device deadline misses.
With preallocated recovery buffers, four simultaneous restarts exhausted quarantine but incurred zero deadline misses; invalidations stayed within slack.
Implement DomainGuard v4’s per-driver quarantine pools and fail-closed admission; rerun delayed-PCIe four-crash stress, checking allocator isolation and deadlines.
Four-crash DomainGuard v4: isolated pools contained delayed DMA, but PCIe drains stalled shared fabric 120 µs; two deadlines missed.
Retain serialized invalidations and preallocated quarantine; withhold v4 certification until PCIe drain interference meets 1 ms bounds.
Partition devices across PCIe roots, reserved memory bandwidth, and cores; isolate driver memory/DMA and mask/reset faults root-locally.
Can root-local resets and memory-bandwidth reservations bound PCIe drain interference within unaffected devices’ 1 ms response-time budgets?
Dedicated PCIe roots and bandwidth reservations bound cross-root drain blocking below 30 µs, preserving 1 ms deadlines during four restarts.
Run RootSplit-4 with four concurrent driver restarts, dedicated PCIe roots and bandwidth reservations; measure cross-root blocking and deadline misses.
RootSplit-4 measured 24 µs maximum cross-root drain blocking and zero unaffected-device deadline misses across 10,000 four-restart trials.
Integrate RootSplit-4 reservations with DomainGuard isolation; certify worst-case shared-resource blocking and 1 ms response times across four restarts.
Integrate DomainGuard v4 with RootSplit-4 PCIe-root and bandwidth partitions; rerun delayed-DMA four-crash tests and response-time analysis.
DomainGuard-RootSplit integration patch assigns driver domains to dedicated PCIe roots and bandwidth partitions, preserving per-driver quarantine and slack-gated invalidations.
Run IntegratedFault-4 on DomainGuard-RootSplit with four concurrent crashes, delayed DMA, and 100-kHz storms; certify unaffected-device 1 ms response bounds.
IntegratedFault-4: 10,000 four-crash trials showed zero escaped CPU/DMA writes or deadline misses; certified unaffected-device response bound was 0.98 ms.
Stress DomainGuard-RootSplit with simultaneous root-local resets and memory-controller saturation; measure cross-root blocking and unaffected-device deadline misses.
Concurrent root-local resets and memory-controller saturation imposed 90 µs cross-root blocking despite reservations, causing four unaffected-device deadline misses.
Can memory-controller bandwidth reservations bound simultaneous root-reset interference without weakening unaffected devices’ 1 ms response-time guarantee?
Dedicated memory-controller service slots and serialized root resets limit additional blocking to 15 µs, preserving 1 ms deadlines.
Implement fixed memory-controller service slots and queued root-local resets; rerun saturation stress measuring added blocking and deadline misses.
Saturation stress: queued resets and controller slots limited added blocking to 12 µs; zero misses, certified response bound 0.992 ms.
Run RefreshCollision-4 with four queued resets, delayed PCIe writes, and worst-phase DRAM refresh; measure slot overruns and deadline misses.
RefreshCollision-4: worst-phase DRAM refresh extended controller-slot blocking to 26 µs, causing three unaffected-device 1 ms deadline misses.
Retain root-local isolation and serialized resets, but defer 1 ms certification until DRAM-refresh blocking is bounded in controller slots.
Physically separate critical-device PCIe roots, DRAM controllers, and cores; isolate restartable drivers with MMU/IOMMU domains and interrupt remapping.
Does physical DRAM-controller separation eliminate refresh-induced deadline misses during four concurrent driver restarts and interrupt storms?
Separate DRAM controllers prevent recovery refresh collisions from increasing critical-device blocking, yielding zero 1 ms misses during four restarts.
Run SplitDRAM-4 with four concurrent restarts, 100-kHz interrupt storms, and worst-phase refresh; measure cross-controller blocking and deadline misses.
SplitDRAM-4: separate controllers avoided refresh collisions, but shared coherence-fabric snoops added 48 µs blocking and caused two 1 ms misses.
Repeat SplitDRAM-4 using noncoherent DMA, uncached recovery buffers, and isolated snoop domains; check four-restart 1 ms response bounds.
SplitDRAM-4 with isolated snoops: 10,000 four-restart trials had zero deadline misses; worst-case unaffected-device response bound was 0.94 ms.
Adopt split controllers, isolated snoops, noncoherent DMA, and uncached buffers; shared snoops missed deadlines, isolated response bound was 0.94 ms.
Integrate adopted controller/snoop isolation with DomainGuard restarts; verify DMA containment and certified 1 ms deadlines during four-crash refresh stress.
Integrate DomainGuard v4 with isolated DRAM controllers, snoop domains, and noncoherent DMA; add uncached per-driver quarantine buffers.
SplitGuard patchset partitions PCIe roots, DRAM controllers, and snoop domains; adds noncoherent DMA, uncached quarantine, and DomainGuard v4 restarts.
Run SplitGuard-Fault4: four crashes, delayed DMA, 100-kHz storms, and worst-phase refresh; verify containment and 1 ms response bound.
SplitGuard-Fault4: 10,000 four-crash trials yielded zero escaped CPU/DMA writes or deadline misses; certified unaffected-device response bound was 0.97 ms.
Adopt SplitGuard with isolated snoops and noncoherent DMA; shared snoops missed deadlines, while integrated four-crash tests certified 0.97 ms.
